title: Streaming Semantics: Visual Guide
outline: 1. Two Clocks Running | event time and processing time drifting apart as network delay rises | processing-time windowing is the streaming form of ingestion-date partitioning, and it looks correct until something is slow

2. One Event, How Many | the same 10:07 event under fixed, sliding and session windows on a timeline | how many windows claim an event is your state and output multiplier — and sessions can merge after the fact, changing the window's identity

3. The Lateness Gate | an event's fate as it arrives further past the watermark, against a one-hour allowed lateness | allowed lateness is measured in event time and every window held open is retained state, so long tails belong in a reconciliation job rather than in window state

4. Panes And The Sink | three panes of one window under accumulating vs discarding, against a summing vs upserting sink | accumulating panes are replacements and discarding panes are deltas, so only two of the four combinations reach the true total of 103

5. Where Once Breaks | a redelivered message through source offsets, internal state, an external call and the sink write | the runner's exactly-once covers its own offsets and state and nothing else, so effectively-once — stable id plus idempotent write — is the guarantee that survives
